# Fitting Generalized Extreme Value Distribution to Asheville Precipitation

### Data Preparation and Package Import 

``` {r initialization}
# Package Import
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(evd)
library(extRemes)

# Data Import
asheville_df <- read.csv("../data/ghcn_roi_daily_data/Asheville.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Data cleaning
## Basic
asheville_df <- asheville_df %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>% # put date in date data format
  filter(!is.na(precipitation)) # Remove any missing precip entries
## Add block maxima (1-year maximum precipitation)
annual_max <- asheville_df %>%
  mutate(year = year(date)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarize(annual_max_precip = max(precipitation, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_days = sum(!is.na(precipitation)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(is.finite(annual_max_precip))
## Check on resulting data:
print(head(annual_max))
cat("Number of years available:", nrow(annual_max), "\n")
ggplot(annual_max, aes(x = annual_max_precip)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 11) +
  labs(title = "Histogram of annual maxima (daily precipitation)", x = "Annual max (mm)", y = "Count")
```

``` {r fitting-GEV-one-day-periods}
# Set random seed for MLE
set.seed(5845)

# evd::fgev uses parameterization (location = mu, scale = sigma > 0, shape = xi)
# Starting values are important; fgev can compute defaults but we pick sensible starts.
x <- annual_max$annual_max_precip

# try a fit with evd
gev_fit_evd <- tryCatch(
  fgev(x, std.err = TRUE),
  error = function(e) {
    message("evd::fgev failed with error: ", e$message, "\nAttempting with initial estimates.")
    # sensible initials: location = mean, log(scale)=log(sd), shape small (0.1)
    fgev(x, start = list(loc = mean(x), scale = sd(x), shape = 0.1), std.err = TRUE)
  }
)

summary(gev_fit_evd)
print(gev_fit_evd$std.err)
# Grab estimates and standard errors
est_evd <- gev_fit_evd$estimate
se_evd  <- gev_fit_evd$std.err # works to get SEs
cat("\nEVD (fgev) estimates:\n")
print(data.frame(parameter = c("loc","scale","shape"), estimate = est_evd, se = se_evd))

# Compute return levels using evd::qgev:
# Return period T years => non-exceedance prob p = 1 - 1/T for annual maxima
return_periods <- c(20, 50, 100)
pvals <- 1 - 1/return_periods
rls_evd <- sapply(pvals, function(p) qgev(p, loc = est_evd["loc"], scale = est_evd["scale"], shape = est_evd["shape"]))
rl_df <- data.frame(return_period = return_periods, return_level = rls_evd)
print(rl_df)
```

``` {r}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# extRemes::fevd 
# fevd does MLE and supports return-level CIs via profile-likelihood
# method = "MLE" is default. set type = "GEV"
gev_fit_ext <- fevd(x, type = "GEV", method = "MLE", units = "years")

print(gev_fit_ext)       # brief
summary(gev_fit_ext)     # more details

# param estimates
params_ext <- gev_fit_ext$results$par
cov_ext <- gev_fit_ext$results$cov
se_ext <- if (!is.null(cov_ext)) sqrt(diag(cov_ext)) else rep(NA, length(params_ext))

gev_summary_ext <- data.frame(
  parameter = names(params_ext),
  estimate  = params_ext,
  se        = se_ext
)

gev_summary_ext

# Return Level & CI
safe_return_level <- function(fit, rp) {
  
  # 1. point estimate
  rl_est <- return.level(fit, return.period = rp)[1]
  
  # ----------------- Try profile likelihood CI -----------------
  ci_proflik <- try(
    ci(fit, type="return.level", return.period = rp, method="proflik"),
    silent = TRUE
  )
  
  if (!inherits(ci_proflik, "try-error") &&
      is.list(ci_proflik) &&
      !is.null(ci_proflik$ci) &&
      length(ci_proflik$ci) == 2 &&
      all(is.finite(ci_proflik$ci))) {
    
    return(data.frame(
      return_period = rp,
      estimate = rl_est,
      lower = ci_proflik$ci[1],
      upper = ci_proflik$ci[2],
      ci_method = "proflik"
    ))
  }
  
  # ----------------- Try delta method CI -----------------
  ci_delta <- try(
    ci(fit, type="return.level", return.period = rp, method="delta"),
    silent = TRUE
  )
  
  if (!inherits(ci_delta, "try-error") &&
      is.list(ci_delta) &&
      !is.null(ci_delta$ci) &&
      length(ci_delta$ci) == 2 &&
      all(is.finite(ci_delta$ci))) {
    
    return(data.frame(
      return_period = rp,
      estimate = rl_est,
      lower = ci_delta$ci[1],
      upper = ci_delta$ci[2],
      ci_method = "delta"
    ))
  }
  
  # ----------------- Fallback: NA bounds -----------------
  return(data.frame(
    return_period = rp,
    estimate = rl_est,
    lower = NA,
    upper = NA,
    ci_method = "none"
  ))
}

return_periods <- c(2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200)

rl_table <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(return_periods, function(rp) safe_return_level(gev_fit_ext, rp))
)

rl_table

# --------- 4. Return Level Plot -------------#
ggplot(rl_table, aes(x = return_period, y = estimate)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue") +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
              alpha = 0.2, fill = "blue",
              na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = return_periods) +
  labs(title = "GEV Return Level Plot",
       x = "Return period (years, log scale)",
       y = "Return level",
       caption = "CIs via profile likelihood (preferred), delta method if needed.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```
